key_insight: ISLA embeds coordinate and unit invariance into a transformer for steady, boundary-driven PDEs while maintaining consistency under mesh refinement.
engineering_relevance: It targets reliable fluid-flow prediction across changes in geometry pose, measurement units, and boundary meshing without treating equivalent physical problems differently.
method: Uses distances and relative angles to learned slice anchors, with no coordinates passed directly to learned operations.
Weights boundary sums by quadrature and normalizes lengths using a boundary-derived scale.
Predicts interior fields through a tree-accelerated learned boundary kernel, with each query independent of other queries.
evidence_signal: Across 2,816 AeroZoo flows, mean reference-scaled velocity and pressure errors were at least 3.1× and 3.3× lower than any baseline’s; on AirfRANS, ISLA ranked second to GLOBE.
watch_item: The reported scope is steady, boundary-driven PDEs; performance on unsteady flows is not established by the abstract.
paper_title: ISLA: A Coordinate-Free, Measure-Weighted Transformer for Boundary-Driven PDEs
